title: Stained-Glass Composition IV
lede: Three tall leaded-glass windows for a house in Alkmaar, made in the movement’s first year: small rectangles of white, yellow, blue, and dark glass arranged in mirrored patterns.
summary: Three leaded windows of small white, yellow, blue, green, ochre, and dark rectangles. Theo van Doesburg, 1917.

source.label: Kröller-Müller Museum: Stained-glass composition IV for the De Lange House, Alkmaar

evidence.note: Inspected the Commons image (1396 × 2135 px, viewed at 1600 px) from Geheugen van Nederland (urn:gvn:ICN01:3492), which shows all three windows on a dark ground. The Kröller-Müller page was found by search and not read.

styles.note: Partial fit: an early De Stijl work that is strictly orthogonal and built from flat colored rectangles, but uses green, ochre, and brown glass and a mirrored, near-symmetric layout that the mature style drops.

context: Jan de Lange commissioned the windows for his house at Wilhelminalaan 2, Alkmaar, where they were installed from early September 1917. Each window measures 287 × 56.5 cm. [Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Theo_van_Doesburg_139.jpg).

The windows passed to the Dutch State (RCE R5533–R5535) and have been on loan to the Kröller-Müller Museum, Otterlo, since 1991. [Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Theo_van_Doesburg_139.jpg).
Wikidata records the work as [Q2460532](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q2460532), dated 1917.
observed: Three tall, narrow panels stand side by side on a dark ground.
Each panel is filled with small rectangles of white glass and of yellow, blue, and very dark glass, divided by thin black lead lines.
The two outer panels repeat the same pattern as mirror images of each other.
The middle panel uses green, ochre, and dark blue glass instead of yellow.
The rectangles form L-shapes and bars that recur down each panel; there are no curves or diagonals.
A small monogram sits at the bottom right.
interpretation: The windows show the style before Mondrian’s large planes: a dense rhythm of small rectangles, closer to a pattern than to a balanced composition.
The lead lines play the part that black lines play in the paintings, which may be one source of the style’s black grid.
borrow: Repeat a small set of rectangular motifs down a tall strip, and mirror the strip for side panels.
Use thin dark dividers between many small cells for a textured band, and keep large planes for main content.

images.alt: Three tall leaded-glass window panels on a dark ground, each filled with small white, yellow, blue, and dark rectangles; the outer panels mirror each other and the middle panel uses green and ochre glass.
images.caption: Theo van Doesburg, Stained-Glass Composition IV, 1917, for the De Lange House, Alkmaar. Dutch State collection, on loan to the Kröller-Müller Museum. Image from [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Theo_van_Doesburg_139.jpg) via Geheugen van Nederland, public domain.

rights.statement: Commons marks the image PD-old. Van Doesburg died in 1931, so the work is public domain in the Netherlands; made in 1917, it is public domain in the United States.
